title: What a map decides — Image Wiki

rules.rule: Design the map at its smallest intended viewing size first, rather than scaling up from a larger version.
rules.evidence: Decide the smallest intended size first, then design at it, not at 200%.

rules.rule: Ensure geometric symbols remain readable when small, while complex symbols require more room to be understood.
rules.evidence: Their practical rule: geometric symbols stay readable when small, complex ones need room.

rules.rule: Use visual contrast as a finite resource where the theme needs to stand out against a low-contrast base.
rules.evidence: Turn contrast up and features separate; turn it down and they read as belonging together, which is precisely why a basemap should be low-contrast.
